newsitem.title: USA: Rymer seeks to eliminate long term debt.
newsitem.headline: Rymer seeks to eliminate long term debt.

text.p: Rymer Foods Inc said Tuesday its directors approved a plan to eliminate its long-term notes through an exchange of existing long-term debt for equity.

The debt for equity recapitalization calls for approval by holders of the majority of the firm's outstanding common stock for the restructuring and issuance of up to 4.3 million shares of new common stock. The new stock will be used to retire at least 95 percent of the company's senior notes, which are its only long-term debt.
Approval of the plan will likely result in a dilution of the current shareholders' equity by 90 percent, it said.

Rymer said the exchange of these notes will eliminate 95 percent of all long term debt from Rymer's capital structure. Rymer said it believes this is necessary to ensure the company's long term viability.

If approved, holders of Rymer's 11 percent senior notes due 2000 will be issued a yet-to-be determined number of shares of Rymer new common stock for each $1,000 pf principal and accrued interest to date.

Rymer said it expects to file within the week a statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission covering details of the proposed exchange. After SEC review, the plan will be submitted to Rymer shareholders and noteholders for approval.
The annual meeting scheduled for April 16, 1997 will be rescheduled when the SEC filing become effective, it said.

"We are optimistic that the financial capitalization of Rymer Foods, our holding company, will parallel the recent progress we have had during the past year with our Rymer Meat subsidiary," said P. Edward Schenk, chairman and president, in a statement.
Rymer supplies portion-control meat to restaurants and institutional foodservice providers.
